The primary projector GUI now contains only global presentation controls, power status and the removable Projection Core.
Use Image Workspace, Item Workspace or Entity Workspace to choose and edit the content being projected.
Apply saves global Scale, Lift, Rotation, Floating, Lighting, Ghost Effect and Tint. Source workspaces save their own content directly.
This handbook is temporary development documentation and is intentionally updated as systems become usable.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.core.5: Netherite: 384 PU · scale 160px · lift 160px · float 32px. The chassis can still impose a lower geometric limit.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.1: Import normalized PNG, JPG, JPEG or WebP assets. The server stores normalized PNG assets by SHA-256 ID.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.2: Current plane chassis expose Front and Back. Back may mirror Front, show Front readable, or use an independent image.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.3: Vertical Flip and Scanlines are image-specific controls and therefore live in this workspace instead of the primary GUI.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.image.4: Mirage Prism now stores independent North/East/South/West image faces. Same Source on All Faces copies North's asset reference without duplicating files.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.1: Click an item onto the virtual Snapshot slot. Mirage copies one serialized visual snapshot and never removes the real item.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.2: Blocks render as 3D blocks, ordinary items use their full 3D item model, and standalone armor targets equipped geometry on the invisible rig.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.item.3: Clearing the virtual slot deletes only the snapshot. There is no obtainable stored item to steal or duplicate.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.1: Craft an Empty Scan Template with paper surrounded by eight iron nuggets, then Shift + right-click one living entity or player. Mirage gives this deliberate scan gesture priority over the target interaction.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.2: Humanoid scans expose Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Main Hand and Off Hand Incoming/Projected channels. Accepting a physical staging item returns the real item immediately; leaving the workspace also returns every leftover staging item, dropping overflow safely.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.3: Horse scans expose Saddle and Body Armor channels. Generic entities keep unsupported visual equipment inside the frozen entity snapshot.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.4: Humanoid projections have persistent pose presets. Pose changes the virtual rig only; scanned body and equipment snapshots stay untouched.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.entity.5: Pose-aware preview fitting and conservative clearance reserve extra room for raised or spread arms.
Scale preserves the source aspect/model proportions. Lift moves the lowest projected point above the emitter.
Rotation controls period, direction and orientation. Floating controls amplitude and either time-cycle or rotation-synced timing.
Ghost Effect changes transparency. Tint applies a hologram color multiplier. Fullbright ignores world light.
Projection Power and clearance must both pass. Debug chassis override is Creative-only and never bypasses Core limits.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.title: Development / Known Boundaries
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.1: Prism is functional for Image and Banner faces. Effigy and Colossal remain future chassis contracts, while Wide/Tall/Field still need their multi-source layout pass.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.2: Optional backpack/accessory/artifact integrations are outside the base scope and will be adapters after the core systems stabilize.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.3: Humanoid pose presets are implemented. Special renderer compatibility and exact species-aware Entity bounds still need refinement.
handbook.mirage_projector.page.dev.4: If a renderer cannot safely support a feature, Mirage should fall back rather than silently corrupt shared render state.

handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: The main projector screen controls presentation. Source workspaces decide what is projected: Image, Item Snapshot, Entity / Humanoid or Banner.
Projection Cores provide power and hard limits. Glass 16 PU, Quartz 32 PU, Amethyst 96 PU, Diamond 192 PU and Netherite 384 PU. Better cores also allow greater Scale, Lift and Floating.
Core and chassis are independent limits. A powerful Core never turns a small chassis into a larger projector. An insufficient Core disables the hologram without deleting its saved configuration.
Image assets are synchronized by asset ID. Item, Banner and Entity equipment sources are virtual snapshots: Mirage records their appearance without storing or consuming the original physical item.
Scale, Lift, Rotation, Floating, Lighting, Ghost Effect and Tint affect presentation. Clearance must also pass before a hologram is active. Creative Debug chassis override never bypasses Core limits.
To scan a living entity, use an Empty Scan Template with Shift + right-click. Entity projections are client-side render reconstructions: no AI, ticking or spawned duplicate entity is created.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.compac: Use Compact for the smallest local holograms: a single icon, item, banner or entity display where the projection should stay close to a tiny emitter.
Chassis limits: 10×10 px envelope, up to 32 px Lift, 4 px Floating amplitude and 1 source.
Compact is best for subtle labels, desk-sized displays and small decorative projections. Choose a larger chassis when readability or physical projection size matters more than footprint.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.displa: Use Display as the standard single-source projector. It gives one balanced square hologram without the specialised multi-source layout of Wide, Tall or Field.
Chassis limits: 16×16 px envelope, up to 48 px Lift, 6 px Floating amplitude and 1 source.
Display is the general-purpose choice for readable images, individual items, banners and ordinary entity showcases when Compact is too restrictive.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.1: Use Wide for horizontal signs, panoramas and side-by-side content. Its chassis is designed around a long landscape footprint.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.2: Chassis limits: 80×32 px envelope, up to 64 px Lift, 8 px Floating amplitude and capacity for 4 sources.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.3: In Image Mode, Wide provides a persistent 4×1 source bank. Scale controls the complete layout while every occupied cell keeps its own image aspect ratio.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.1: Use Tall for vertical signage, portrait-oriented art and stacked content where height matters much more than width.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.2: Chassis limits: 32×80 px envelope, up to 96 px Lift, 12 px Floating amplitude and capacity for 4 sources.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.3: In Image Mode, Tall provides a persistent 1×4 source bank. Scale controls the whole vertical layout and each cell preserves its source aspect ratio.
Use Field for large square displays, image walls and mosaic-style installations. It is the current planar chassis for the broadest multi-source area.
Chassis limits: 80×80 px envelope, up to 96 px Lift, 16 px Floating amplitude and capacity for 9 sources.
In Image Mode, Field provides a persistent 3×3 source bank. Clearance reserves the full layout footprint even when only some cells are populated.
Use Prism for a freestanding holographic display that can be read from several directions instead of one flat front/back plane.
Chassis limits: 48×48 px envelope, up to 96 px Lift, 12 px Floating amplitude and capacity for 4 sources.
Image and Banner modes expose North, East, South and West faces. Same Source on All Faces reuses North on every side. Prism intentionally has no top or bottom face.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: Plane Image projection modes are explicit. Front shows only the Front asset; Back shows only the Back asset; Mirrored reuses Front on the rear as a mirror; Readable reuses Front but corrects the rear orientation; Independent uses separate Front and Back assets.
